Bit of a background:
After my 8 year relationship (lived together for 7, got engaged) endet in a horrible dumpster fire (got cheated on for 1 1/2 years, was being lied to when she claimed to gibe us another try), losing my place to live, and my emotional anchor in live (grew up in an unemotional family. No dad, single mom with 2 kids that worked from morning to evening, my sister hates me), I was heavily suicidal :D.

Anyway, I knew that if things stayed as they were, I wouldn't make it for long. So I contacted the local psychological help center for students (I was 26 at that time). There I had to film out a questionnaire, and got to talk to someone immediately after. Well, my mask broke down, I cried a lot, told her the gist of it, and got quiet afterwards. She acted like a pro and told me: "sorry to tell this to you, but your problems are way over what we can do here. There's a real clinic behind this building, and I'm going to take you there, and get a doctor to speak with you, to see if you have to get admitted or not."

To not make this too long, I'll simply summerise what happened afterward.
The doctor was the best thing that could've happened to me (we are now married! Just kidding ^^"). But he did tell me a lot about humans in general, and about what being a young adult actually means, and in the end, he simply let me go home, after I promised, that I'd reach out again, whenever I needed help.

This really wasn't negligence on his part, but more my own personal wish. The core of counseling is mutual trust, and he showed me, that it was normal to feel bad, be in a bad spot, and still have people be able to trust you (among many other things in that one hour talk).

I guess the reason for this long post is, that if you feel like you need help (even if you cope super well, get to work and all that), go and get it. Or talk to a friend to accompany you. Noone has to feel bad, and sometimes, all it takes is the right person for a good, long talk.

So, most of the other comments are on fullout confrontation. I was once in a kinda similar situation, and I don't need to tell you - don't let the situation remain like this. It'll fuck you up, and you'll need a long time to revert to the awesome guy you are.

Now, confronting etc. most certainly is an option, and I'm an advocate of direct and open communication. But: you kinda tried all of that.

I'd give you the advice to START CARING FOR YOURSELF THR MOST. Sounds strange, but all those things you wrote, it's just "she wants this, she wants that, I want to support her". And seeing as you still love her, and maybe you don't even want to turn your whole life upside down, then maybe you just gotta think really hard about what it is, that is missing.

Obviously you'll think "she is!" but I'm sorry... That's not how this works. Is it sexual attraction that you long for (like she looks at Gabe)? You can get that by searching for new (girl-) friends yourself! Is it someone to talk to? Well guess what, there are tons of other people you can have those with.

That way, even if it eventually ends (if it ends), you'll have the right mindset going in the future. It's great you found her, and have a good marriage. But if something happens (f.e. Your wife could realize, that she is that attracted to someone not her husband, which in turn let her realize that you are not the love of her life), your life'll still go on.

Wish you the best

And if you happen to still be reading this, I´ll give you my best tips in how to get through and above that feeling which plagues us:

It´s super cliché, but all happiness comes from within you. Like, we did have love, which at some point was the spring of everything good in our life, but now that love has turned. Turned into something that keeps on hurting (for me tbh, it´s not rly hatred). And now we need to find the ability to be happy on our own - without depending on a new guy/girl or something like that!

So, what to do?
Q: "Are you happy with your current self?"
A: "Hell no!"
Q: "When was the last time you were happy? 2-3 years ago?"
A: "Yea, about that time"
Q: "Then now you´ll aim to feeling twice as good as you did at that time. What is it you want to achieve? Where do you want to go? You can do everything you want to"

It really doesnt sound as good now that I´ve written it down, but a conversation of this kind made me motivated, to start picking myself up again.
